name: William Tolbert
role: Ran the Elk saloon in Little Missouri; later in the National Park country
bio: William Tolbert was running the Elk saloon in Little Missouri in June 1885, and in December he went west with Charles Jolly. By August 1886 he was with Jack Matlock at the National Park stage line.

moments.label: Running the Elk in first-class style
Reported at the National Park stage line

mentions: …the Medora stage Tuesday were Mr. and Mrs. N. C. Ludgen, H. M. Janlund, E. D. Morse, M. Franke, O. Kinley, W. Tolbert.
Tuesday's stage from Deadwood made the trip in 36 hours and 5 minutes. If you want to go to the Hills in a hurry, take the M. S. & F. Co.'s route.
…open the Elk Saloon in Little Missouri tomorrow, and will be pleased to have my friends call and see me.  Wm. Talbert
William Tolbert is conducting the Elk in first-class style and would be pleased to see his friends at all times. Give him a call.
Wm. Tolbert went west with Chas. Jolly last week. They expect to secure positions on the Benton & Billings stage line for the winter.
A letter from Jack Matlock informs us that he is driving for the National Park stage line, that Wm. Tolbert is also there and that Chas. Jolly is on the Billings and Benton stage line.
